_instructions: Locale-agnostic starter template for an appeals navigator. Replace every [REPLACE] value with jurisdiction-specific information and remove all underscore-prefixed metadata keys before publishing. This template illustrates questions, date inputs, conditional branches, and terminal checklists. It does not constitute legal advice.

start._note: Entry point. Ask the user which court or locality has jurisdiction over the case.
start.text: [REPLACE: Ask which court, locality, or division handled the case.]

judgment_notice._note: Determine whether the user has received formal notice of the judgment or order.
judgment_notice.text: [REPLACE: Ask whether formal notice of the judgment or order has been served.]

notice_date._note: Date input demonstrates how an author can collect a date that may affect a later deadline calculation.
notice_date.text: [REPLACE: Ask for the date formal notice was served.]

service_method._note: Determine whether service occurred by a method that changes the applicable deadline.
service_method.text: [REPLACE: Ask how the notice was served.]

deadline_check._note: Example branch node. The host application or bundle-specific logic must establish deadlineExpired before this node is reached.

deadline_expired._note: Generic expired-deadline outcome. Replace with the actual jurisdiction-specific remedy.

items.text: [REPLACE: Explain what happens when the ordinary appeal deadline has expired and identify any available late-appeal or extension procedure.]
[REPLACE: Direct the user to qualified legal assistance.]
[REPLACE: Provide the official court or government resource for late appeals.]

post_judgment_motion._note: Determine whether another post-judgment proceeding may affect the appeal path.
post_judgment_motion.text: [REPLACE: Ask whether the user has filed or is considering a post-judgment motion.]

options.label: [REPLACE: Yes — I have a pending motion]

motion_type._note: Generic motion-type example. Replace options with the motions recognized in the target jurisdiction.
motion_type.text: [REPLACE: Ask what type of post-judgment motion was filed.]

motion_warning._note: Illustrates a jurisdiction-specific procedural warning that should only be retained if legally accurate.
motion_warning.text: [REPLACE: Explain any procedural consequence of the selected motion and ask the user to acknowledge it.]

stay_question._note: Determine whether the user needs relief preventing enforcement while the appeal is pending.
stay_question.text: [REPLACE: Ask whether the user needs a stay or other interim relief while the appeal is pending.]

security_question._note: Generic example for jurisdictions where a bond, undertaking, deposit, or other security may affect a stay.
security_question.text: [REPLACE: Ask whether the user can satisfy any applicable security or undertaking requirement.]

options.label: [REPLACE: Yes — I can satisfy the requirement]

alternative_relief._note: Only retain if the jurisdiction provides an alternative to a standard security requirement.
alternative_relief.text: [REPLACE: Ask whether the user wants information about an alternative form of relief.]

get_help._note: Generic escalation path when the user's situation cannot safely be resolved by the navigator.

items.text: [REPLACE: Explain why the situation requires individualized legal assistance.]

checklist_appeal._note: Generic terminal checklist demonstrating how a jurisdiction author can convert the decision tree into concrete actions.

items.text: [REPLACE: File the required notice or initiating document with {{court_name}} before the applicable deadline.]
[REPLACE: Serve the required parties according to the jurisdiction's service rules.]
[REPLACE: Request the record, transcript, or other materials required for the appeal.]
[REPLACE: If you are seeking a stay, file the required stay application and supporting papers.]
[REPLACE: Keep copies of every filing, proof of service, receipt, and court order.]
[REPLACE: Contact {{legal_aid_name}} for assistance if you need help understanding or completing the process.]
